custom_logic_notes: Core signal generation uses Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification via external svMachineTool.ex5 library. Two separate SVMs are trained at initialization: one for buy signals, one for sell signals. Training inputs are generated from 7 technical indicator values over N_DataPoints bars. Training outputs are generated by simulating hypothetical trades (BUY or SELL) with given stopLoss/takeProfit levels over a maximum duration of 'hours' hours. The SVM is trained with a tolerance parameter. On each new bar, classify() is called on both SVMs using current indicator values to produce buy/sell signals. Stop loss and take profit are implemented as pending orders (SellStop/BuyStop for SL, SellLimit/BuyLimit for TP) rather than built-in SL/TP, with ticket numbers cached in a dynamic array to pair SL and TP orders. When one order triggers, OnTrade() searches the cache to find and delete the matching counterpart order.
backtest_data_needs: Any symbol with 5-digit pricing, any timeframe, 730 days
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement SVM signal generation in Python: 1) Compute 7 indicator features per bar using ta-lib or pandas-ta. 2) Generate training labels by simulating hypothetical trades: for each historical bar, check if a buy/sell with given SL/TP would have hit TP before SL within 'hours' duration. 3) Train sklearn.svm.SVC (or similar) on indicator features vs labels with tolerance parameter. 4) At each bar, use trained SVM to classify current indicator values as buy/sell signal. The pending order SL/TP management with ticket cache must be reimplemented as paired SL/TP orders that cancel each other when one triggers. The Pip_Size() function should be replaced with proper pip calculation based on symbol digits.
